utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the registrar call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-98-30-I, the Prosecutor versus Miroslav Kvocka, Milojica Kos, Mladen Radic and Zoran Zigic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Niemann, and I appear with my colleagues, Mr. Keegan and Mr. Waydaratne, and Ms. Reynders is the case manager for the Prosecution, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. For the Defence in the order of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honour, my name is Krstan Simic, Defence counsel for Mr. Miroslav Kvocka. My co-counsel is unable to attend today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honour, my name is Sarko Nikolic, attorney representing Milojica Kos. To my left, my co-counsel, Ms. Jelena Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Good morning, Your Honours. I am attorney Toma Fila, and together with co-counsel Mr. Petrovic, I represent the accused Mladjo Radic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, my name is Simo Tosic, representing the accused Zoran Zigic. To my right, my co-counsel, Jelena Lopicic, attorney from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Tosic, let me address you first. I see that your client is wearing dark glasses. Now, that is not normally allowed in a court. Is there a particular reason why he is wearing those glasses?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, the main reason is the medical condition of my client, since light disturbs him, and he is advised to wear glasses in such conditions. That is the only reason, no other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Tosic, then if he wishes to apply to the Court to wear dark glasses and there is a medical reason for that, he must make a formal application, or you, on his behalf, must make a formal application, and it must be supported, if there is a medical reason, by a medical report. So before the next appearance, if you want, or if your client wants to wear dark glasses, then he must formally apply. Is that understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Yes, Your Honours. We will do as you have advised us for the next hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, let me turn next to the accused to make sure that they can hear what is being said in a language which they understand. Can you all hear?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If there is any difficulty during the proceedings or any proceedings before this Trial Chamber, if you have any difficulty hearing, will you indicate straightaway? Now, if I could turn to Defence counsel, please? This appearance has been listed for the accused to enter pleas to new charges on the amended indictment, and there are some preliminary matters which I need to deal with first, and to comply with the Rules, I must ask you first to confirm the following: That your client has received a copy of the indictment in a language which he understands; that you have had the opportunity of going through it with him; that he understands it and is in a position to enter a plea. Perhaps I can ask you in the indictment order to confirm those matters? Mr. Simic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, my client and I have received the indictment. He understands the indictment, and he is quite prepared to enter a plea today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, my answer to all your questions is in the affirmative.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, my answer is "Yes."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, my answer is "Yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. And the next matter is this: The Rules do allow the accused the right to have the indictment read out in court in full, but they also may waive that right, and before we turn to the plea, I must ask you this: Do any of your clients want the indictment read out in full, or will you waive the right? Perhaps someone could give me an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, our clients do not insist on the indictment being read, and we can proceed with the pleas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Fila. Let the accused stand. I am now going to read the counts to you. Will you kindly confine your answers to each count, either "guilty" or "not guilty" to each? Count 1, Messrs. Kvocka, Kos, and Radic, a crime against humanity punishable under Articles 5(h) (persecutions on political, racial or religious grounds), and 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Mr. Kvocka, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED KVOCKA: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I plead not guilty. I am absolutely not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kos? THE ACCUSED KOS: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Radic? THE ACCUSED RADIC: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Zoran Zigic, Count 1, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(h) (persecution on political, racial or religious grounds) and 7(1) of the Statute. Mr. Zigic, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED ZIGIC: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Count 2, a crime against humanity, Messrs. Kvocka, Kos, and Radic, punishable under Articles 5(i) (inhumane acts) and 7 (1) and 7(3) of the Statute. Mr. Kvocka, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED KVOCKA: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I am absolutely not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kos? THE ACCUSED KOS: (Interpretation) Your Honours, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Radic? THE ACCUSED RADIC: (Interpretation) Your Honours, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Zoran Zigic, Count 2, crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(i) (inhumane acts) and 7(1) of the Statute. Mr. Zigic, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED ZIGIC: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Miroslav Kvocka, Milojica Kos, and Mladen Radic, on Count 3, a violation of the laws or customs of war, (outrages upon personal dignity, as recognised by Article 3(1)(c) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949) punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute. Mr. Kvocka, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED KVOCKA: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kos? THE ACCUSED KOS: (Interpretation) Your Honours, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Radic? THE ACCUSED RADIC: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: On the same count, Zoran Zigic, a similar offence, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as I have already read out previously, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute. Mr. Zigic, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED ZIGIC: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Messrs. Kvocka, Kos, and Radic, Count 4, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(a) (murder) and 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Mr. Kvocka, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED KVOCKA: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I am absolutely not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kos? THE ACCUSED KOS: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Radic? THE ACCUSED RADIC: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Count 5, a violation of the laws or customs of war, (murder, as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949) punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute. Mr. Kvocka, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED KVOCKA: (Interpretation) No, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kos? THE ACCUSED KOS: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Radic? THE ACCUSED RADIC: (Interpretation) Your Honours, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Zoran Zigic, Count 6, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(a) (murder) and 7(1) of the Statute. Mr. Zigic, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED ZIGIC: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Count 7, a violation of the laws or customs of war (murder, as recognised by Article (3)(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949) punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute. Mr. Zigic, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED ZIGIC: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Miroslav Kvocka, Milojica Kos, and Mladen Radic, Count 8, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(f) (torture) and 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute. Mr. Kvocka, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED KVOCKA: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kos? THE ACCUSED KOS: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Radic? THE ACCUSED RADIC: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Count 10, a violation of the laws or customs of war, (cruel treatment, as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949) punishable under Articles 3, 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute. Mr. Kvocka, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED KVOCKA: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I am absolutely not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kos? THE ACCUSED KOS: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Radic? THE ACCUSED RADIC: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Zoran Zigic, Count 11, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(f) (torture) and 7(1) of the Statute. Mr. Zigic, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED ZIGIC: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Count 12, a violation of the laws or customs of war, (torture, as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949) punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute. Mr. Zigic, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED ZIGIC: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Count 13, a violation of the laws or customs of war, (cruel treatment, as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949) punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute. Mr. Zigic, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED ZIGIC: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mladen Radic, Count 14, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(f) (torture) and 7(1) of the Statute. Mr. Radic, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED RADIC: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Count 15, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(g) (rape) and 7(1) of the Statute. Mr. Radic, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED RADIC: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Count 16, a violation of the laws or customs of war, (torture, as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949) punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute. Mr. Radic, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED RADIC: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Count 17, a violation of the laws or customs of war, (outrages upon personal dignity, as recognised by Article 3(1)(c) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949) punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Mr. Radic, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED RADIC: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Let the accused remain seated. Mr. Niemann, there are various outstanding matters in this case. There are motions outstanding, there are the questions of a timetable.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It may, in fact, be more convenient -- it may be more convenient to discuss those, or at least some of them, in a Status Conference which we propose to hold immediately after this appearance.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I think that would be appropriate, Your Honour, yes. There are a number of matters that we need to discuss, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The only matter which the Rules require us to consider, the other matter, is the question of a date for trial, and it must be said that at the moment, this case is clearly not ready for trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: There are a number of outstanding motions to be dealt with, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. And again, it may be more convenient to deal with all of those in a Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I think it might be. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honour, I apologise in advance if I am mistaken, but it seems to me that Count number 9 has not been entered in the record. Perhaps it is due to an omission on my part, but Count 9 was left out. There is 8 and there is 10. But if I am mistaken, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I certainly intended that it should be put. If there is any doubt about it, it can be put again. I see the record is being checked.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, it appears that it hasn't been read. I do apologise. I should have been paying for attention to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If it has been overlooked -- thank you, Mr. Fila, for drawing it to our attention. If it has been overlooked, let it be put again. Count 9, Mr. Kvocka, Mr. Kos, and Mr. Radic, please stand. There is no need for Mr. Zigic to stand. There is no need for him to stand. It is the other three accused. Count 9, charges of violation of the laws and customs of war (torture, as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949) punishable under Articles 3, 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute. Mr. Kvocka, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED KVOCKA: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kos? THE ACCUSED KOS: (Interpretation) Your Honours, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And Mr. Radic? THE ACCUSED RADIC: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. If you would like to sit down? Are there any other matters which counsel may wish to raise before we go into a closed Status Conference? As I say, what I propose is that in the Status Conference we discuss the timetable for this case, including any outstanding motions which have to be resolved. But that apart, are there any other matters which counsel would like to raise? I will take --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I apologise again for asking for the floor a second time, but I think that we need to clarify a point from the beginning. I am referring to the name of Mr. Radic. His name is Mladjo Radic. In the indictment, it says Mladen. I think it would be desirable for the Prosecution to correct this for purposes of identification. It is not a big issue, but after all, I think we have to have the name correctly, whether he is guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. It can be amended.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Our information was that that was a street name or nickname. That is how we understood it, and so that is why the indictment reads the way it does. But Mr. Fila has informed us this morning that, in fact, Mladjo is the name he uses, and so we would apply to amend the indictment in conformity with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, if there is no objection, let the indictment be amended. Yes. That being all the matters which have to be discussed at this appearance, the Chamber will now move into a Status Conference, a closed session, to discuss the other matters relating to the case. Can we do that? (Closed session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: status conference

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: at 12.02 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 9th day of March, 1998.
